data.headline: QQQ’s discount-rate backdrop eased by five basis points
data.summary: The US ten-year Treasury yield fell to 4.90% on November 4 from 4.95% on November 3. Holding cash flows and risk premiums fixed, a lower discount rate raises their present value. The change is relevant to growth-company valuation, while the earnings and equity-price inputs remain open.

bull.text: The ten-year benchmark declined by 5 basis points. Valuation scenarios for distant cash flows become more supportive under the explicit assumption that earnings expectations and equity risk premiums are unchanged.

bear.text: At 4.90%, the ten-year yield still contributes materially to discount rates. The 30-year benchmark was 5.28%, retaining a higher long-maturity hurdle for very distant cash flows.

watch.text: Nasdaq-mini futures on October 27 showed asset managers net long 65,381 contracts and leveraged funds net long 2,301. The older weekly report cannot establish their positions after the November rate changes.

limitations: The discount-rate channel is conditional. QQQ prices, index cash-flow revisions, analyst expectations and option-implied volatility remain unavailable.
The November 4 US rates precede the November 5 Bank of England announcement. Nasdaq futures and QQQ share holdings have different instruments and units.
